articles.excerpt: The Ben & Jerry's Foundation announced it will shut down, citing an ongoing legal disagreement with its parent company, Unilever.

Beginner.text:

Ben & Jerry's is a famous ice cream company. It is known for caring about social issues. In 2000, a large company called Unilever bought Ben & Jerry's. When Unilever bought it, they agreed that Ben & Jerry's would keep its special mission. This meant Ben & Jerry's could still decide on its social goals.

But a problem started. Ben & Jerry's did not want its ice cream sold in certain places in Israel. The independent board of Ben & Jerry's felt this was important for their values. However, Unilever, the parent company, decided to sell the business to a local company in Israel anyway. This caused a legal dispute, which means they went to court to solve the problem.

The Foundation gets its money from Ben & Jerry's profits. Because of this big fight, the Foundation has decided it cannot continue its work. It has been helping people for over 30 years. Its closure means less help for many important causes.

The Foundation's statement indicates that the protracted legal dispute has created an environment where it can no longer effectively fulfill its mission.
